pooled_72h_no_monotonicity.note: Monotonicity not imposed. Both arms are trimmed, so neither arm's stratum risk is identified and the interval is uninformative by construction for a rare binary outcome.

monotonicity_tipping_72h.description: Monotonicity would have to fail for 1.58% of the discharged opioid group (patients discharged after an opioid who would have been admitted after a dopamine antagonist) before the always-discharged lower bound reaches 1.0. The outcome is rare, so the one-sided bound is fragile to small departures from the assumption.

tipping_point_72h.description: The selected (discharged) opioid group would have to have a return risk 1.78 times lower than the always-discharged opioid population, with no corresponding distortion in the dopamine-antagonist arm, for the observed association to be entirely selection. Equivalently, the always-discharged share of the discharged dopamine-antagonist group would have to fall from its estimated 0.731 to 0.56 for the always-discharged lower bound to reach the null.
